_meta.legal_basis: Indian Contract Act 1872 + Transfer of Property Act 1882 + Interest Act 1978 + state Money-Lenders Acts + Negotiable Instruments Act 1881
_meta.notes: Loan Agreement between private parties or NBFC/Bank. Interest Act 1978 governs interest. Each state has Money-Lenders Act regulating private lending - registration may be required for habitual lenders. SARFAESI Act applies to secured creditors (banks/NBFCs registered). Stamp duty significant on loan agreements (often 0.1-0.5% of loan value).

title: Loan Agreement

mandatory_clauses.title: Loan Amount and Currency
mandatory_clauses.content: The Lender agrees to lend and the Borrower agrees to borrow a sum of INR {{principal_amount}} (Rupees in words) (the 'Loan').

mandatory_clauses.title: Purpose of Loan
mandatory_clauses.content: The Loan shall be utilised solely for {{purpose}}. The Borrower shall not divert funds for any other purpose without the Lender's prior written consent.

mandatory_clauses.title: Interest
mandatory_clauses.content: The Loan shall carry interest at {{interest_rate}}% per annum, {{interest_type}} basis, compounded {{interest_compounding}}, computed on the outstanding principal. Interest shall be payable in accordance with the Repayment Schedule.

mandatory_clauses.title: Default / Penal Interest
mandatory_clauses.content: In the event of any default in payment of any instalment or interest, the Borrower shall pay additional default interest at {{default_interest_rate}}% per annum on the overdue amount, without prejudice to other remedies.

mandatory_clauses.title: Security and Creation of Security Interest
subclauses: Equitable/registered mortgage of immovable property (TPA S.58-104)
Hypothecation of movables (filing of charge with ROC if Borrower is company - S.77 Cos Act)

mandatory_clauses.title: Consequences of Default
subclauses: Filing recovery suit / Section 138 NI Act on bounced cheques

mandatory_clauses.title: Taxes (TDS u/s 194A on interest, GST if NBFC)
Governing Law and Jurisdiction
mandatory_clauses.content: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of India. Courts at {{jurisdiction_city}} shall have exclusive jurisdiction.

mandatory_clauses.title: Schedules - Repayment Schedule, Security Documents, Promissory Note

prompt_context.system_role: You are drafting a Loan Agreement under Indian law. Comply with Interest Act 1978, state Money-Lenders Acts, TPA for security creation. For company borrower, ensure charge filing under S.77 Cos Act. Interest rate must not be usurious.
drafting_rules: Interest rate must be specified clearly. Avoid usurious rates - state Money-Lenders Acts often cap interest for private lenders.
Default/penal interest typically 2-4% additional. Courts have struck down excessive penal interest as unconscionable.
For corporate borrower: charge filing under S.77 Cos Act 2013 within 30 days, in Form CHG-1.
Security: TPA S.58-104 for mortgage. Registered mortgage requires registration under Registration Act 1908 if value > INR 100.
Equitable mortgage by deposit of title deeds: permitted in notified towns under S.58(f) TPA - no registration but stamp duty applies.
Hypothecation: SARFAESI Act applies for banks/NBFCs. Private lenders rely on contract + civil suit.
Personal guarantee: separate guarantee deed under S.126 Contract Act.
Stamp duty on loan agreement: state-specific, typically 0.1-0.5% of loan value (ad valorem). Mortgage deed higher.
TDS on interest u/s 194A at 10% (subject to thresholds).
NBFC / Bank lenders: RBI regulations apply.
Cross-border ECB: FEMA + RBI ECB Master Direction applies - check tenure, AAR, end-use restrictions.
Promissory note as separate document - stamped under Stamp Act Article 49.
Post-dated cheques: enforceability under S.138 NI Act on dishonour.
Money-Lenders Acts: in Bihar, UP, etc., registration may be required for private lenders if making it a business.
prompt_context.tone: Formal banking-legal, precise on financial terms.

relevantActs.act: Recovery of Debts Due to Banks and Financial Institutions Act 1993

filing_checklist: Execute on stamp paper of ad valorem value per state Stamp Act.
If mortgage: register the mortgage deed with Sub-Registrar within 4 months (Registration Act).
If corporate borrower: file Form CHG-1 within 30 days for creation of charge (S.77 Cos Act).
If S.185 issue (loan to director): comply with conditions or avoid.
Deduct TDS u/s 194A on interest paid (if applicable).
Maintain loan ledger, post-dated cheques, security documents.
For corporate borrower: ensure within S.180 borrowing power limits (else SR).
For ECB: file Form ECB with AD Bank, obtain LRN.

validation_rules.check: Within state money-lenders cap or reasonable for institutional
Security type, asset description, perfection steps

validation_rules.rule: S.77 Cos Act compliance if corporate
validation_rules.check: Charge filing referenced for company borrower
